mode: Built-in image generation: style-transfer edits of current atlases, using the older realistic atlases as supporting references.

prompts.divine_dog_totality: Use case: style-transfer. Edit target is image 1 (CURRENT Minecraft UV texture atlas); image 2 is ONLY an older more realistic style reference. Produce a middle ground between these styles, not a photorealistic surface and not coarse pixel art. Crisp hand-painted game textures with medium-fine pixel clusters, richer subtle shading, 8-12 shades per material and restrained fine detail. Intended 512x512 atlas, 128px per material tile. Keep EXACTLY the first image's 4x4 equal-square edge-to-edge tile layout and material identities. Preserve all first-image eye, mouth and symbol shapes, colors, scale and centers perfectly; do not copy the old reference's incorrect symbol or background variants. Flat diffuse textures, not a rendered sphere or character. No perspective, cast lighting, labels, text, borders, padding or gutters. Every tile fills its square completely. Charcoal wolf fur, off-white fur, slate gray skin, pale gray fur across row1. Restore subtle short individual hair details within medium-size pixel tufts, but avoid huge feather-like strands, leaf shapes and strong directional waves. Row2 ivory claw, black fur, amber vertical-pupil eye, dark-red mouth with two horizontal lines. Row3 crimson, SIX red forehead dots on charcoal in the exact current arrangement, rose tongue, dark paw pads. Row4 matte black nose, charcoal mane, offwhite teeth, same six dots on red. Keep dark fur dark, ivory matte with fine growth ridges not cracked stone. The result should be perceptibly more detailed and gently shaded than current image 1 while still clearly a polished Minecraft creature texture.
